# Audio fixture provenance

This directory documents the non-personal audio fixture set required by
[Task 8, Step 1](../../../docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-09-turn-detection-and-visible-answers.md)
of the turn detection and visible answers plan.

**No audio files are checked into this directory yet.** This environment has
no microphone, speaker loopback, or speech synthesis capability, so no real
or synthetic speech audio could be recorded or generated here. This file
records what a real fixture set must contain so a person or a machine with
audio hardware or a text-to-speech engine can produce it and drop the files
next to this README without changing the acceptance procedure.

## Format requirements

Fixtures must match what `src/audio/pcm-worklet.js` and `src/audio/capture.js`
actually produce and what `src/services/speech.service.js` actually consumes:

- Sample rate: 16000 Hz (the `PcmResampler` in `pcm-worklet.js` resamples any
  input rate down to a fixed `16000`).
- Channels: mono (the worklet downmixes all input channels by averaging them
  before resampling).
- Sample format: signed 16-bit PCM (`Int16Array`, clamped to `[-32768, 32767]`).
- Frame size: captured and posted in 320-sample (20 ms) blocks, but a fixture
  file itself can be one contiguous WAV; the frame size only matters for
  anyone replaying it through the live worklet in real time.
- Container: uncompressed WAV (`RIFF`/`WAVE`, `fmt ` chunk describing
  16-bit PCM mono at 16000 Hz) is the simplest format that needs no decoding
  before being fed to a speech provider or replayed as system audio.

## Required fixtures (one WAV per row)

These map directly to the pause-scenario table in the plan's Task 8, Step 2
and to `docs/testing/turn-detection-acceptance.md`'s Step 2 section, which
also lists which deterministic test already covers each case with a
simulated clock in lieu of real audio.

| File | Content | Pause between parts | Expected combined transcript | Expected question count |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| `continuous-question.wav` | One uninterrupted question | 0.5 s (mid-sentence breath, not a turn boundary) | "Can you explain how a hash map resolves collisions?" | 1 |
| `natural-planning-pause.wav` | A question split by a thinking pause | 2.0 s | "Explain how transformers work and how they are trained." | 1 |
| `boundary-margin.wav` | A question split just under the 3000 ms silence window | 2.8 s | "What is the time complexity of quicksort in the average and worst case?" | 1 |
| `separate-question.wav` | Two distinct questions | 4.0 s | Two separate transcripts, not joined | 2 |
| `slow-second-transcription.wav` | A question split by a 2.0 s pause, where the second segment is deliberately noisy or long enough that transcription takes longer than the silence window | 2.0 s (acoustic), transcription of the second segment settles after the 3000 ms deadline would otherwise have fired | One combined question, released only once the second segment's transcript settles | 1 |

Each file's duration should be long enough to contain natural speech for its
row (roughly 4 to 12 seconds total, depending on question length) plus the
specified pause, recorded or synthesized at the pause length listed above
within +/- 100 ms so the fixture actually exercises the intended side of the
3000 ms default silence window (`AUTO_ANSWER_SILENCE_MS` in `env.example`).

## Non-personal, synthetic provenance

Fixtures must not contain any real person's voice, likeness, or personal
speech recorded from a live interview. Acceptable sources:

- Text-to-speech synthesis of the example questions above, using a
  synthetic/non-cloned voice (for example, a local TTS engine or a
  synthesized-voice cloud service whose terms permit redistribution of the
  generated audio in a test fixture).
- A generic, purpose-recorded voice reading only the scripted example
  questions above, from someone who consents to the recording being
  committed to this repository as a test fixture.

Whoever generates these fixtures should record here (by editing this table)
the exact generation method, tool/version, and date, so the provenance
stays auditable:

| File | Generated by | Tool/version | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _(none yet)_ | | | |

## Why this environment could not produce them

This task was executed in a sandboxed, headless agent environment with no
audio input device, no speaker output, and no bundled text-to-speech engine
or network access to one. Recording real speech or synthesizing speech audio
was not possible here. The deterministic pause-timing and reasoning-filter
behavior these fixtures would exercise live is already covered by simulated-
clock unit tests (see `docs/testing/turn-detection-acceptance.md`); this
README exists so that coverage gap is explicit and actionable rather than
silently assumed.
